analysis.title: Target Corp. (TGT): First Take: 3Q earnings beat; FY26 guidance raised
key_insights: Target reported 3Q26 adjusted EPS of $2.65 including tariff refunds. Excluding refunds, EPS was $2.15 vs GS $2.01 and consensus (FactSet) $2.08. The tariff refund contributed $0.50 per share.
Same-store sales (SSS) rose 5.6% vs consensus of +3.7% and GS at +2.7%. Traffic was +5.0% and ticket +0.6%. Store comp rose 4.6% and digital comp rose 9.8%.
Net sales grew y/y in the majority of core merchandising categories, while apparel declined. November-to-date net sales are in line with company guidance and accelerated from October.
FY26 net sales growth guidance was raised to a range around +6% from around +5%, vs GS and consensus at +5.2%.
FY26 operating margin guidance is around 6.2% including a ~1.1 ppt tariff refund benefit. Excluding refunds this implies about 5.1%, vs prior guidance of about 50 bps higher y/y from 4.6% in FY25.

FY26 EPS guidance is $10.65-11.40 including $2.14 of tariff refund benefits recognized to date. Excluding refunds the range is $8.51-9.26 vs prior $8.25-9.25 and GS at $8.79. Guidance excludes any future tariff refunds.

Gross margin was 30.5% including a 1.1 ppt tariff refund benefit. Excluding refunds it was ~29.4% vs the consensus-aligned estimate of 28.9%, up ~120 bps y/y. Drivers were lapping last year's elevated markdowns and tariff rates, non-merchandise sales growth and supply chain productivity, partly offset by freight and fuel costs, value investments and category mix.

SG&A rose 10.2% y/y. The expense ratio was 21.9% (+61 bps y/y) vs GS 21.5% and consensus 21.4%, due to higher incentive compensation, more store labor hours and store investments, partly offset by sales leverage.
EBIT was $1.7bn including a $301mn tariff refund benefit. Excluding the benefit, EBIT of $1,371mn was above GS $1,256mn and consensus $1,307mn.
Inventory grew 8.4% y/y vs a retail sales increase of 6.9%.
Target expects to invest $5-6bn in capex in 2027.
The stock was down ~2% pre-market. GS is Neutral with a 12-month price target of $161, against a $159.53 price (0.9% upside).

market_movers.rationale: GS stays Neutral with a $161 12-month target based on bear/base/bull relative multiples of 60%/70%/75%. The target is unchanged from the 20 Aug 2026 level and implies 0.9% upside to the $159.53 price.

earnings_insights: TGT 3Q26 (reported 11/18): adjusted EPS $2.65 reported including tariff refunds, $2.15 excluding refunds, vs GS estimate $2.01 and consensus (FactSet) $2.08.
TGT 3Q26 SSS +5.6% reported vs consensus +3.7% and GS estimate +2.7%. Traffic +5.0% vs GS +2.5%, ticket +0.6% vs GS +0.2%.
TGT 3Q26 retail sales $26,449mn (+6.9% y/y) vs GS estimate $25,832mn. Total sales $27,067mn (+7.1% y/y) vs GS $26,454mn (excluding tariff refunds).
TGT 3Q26 gross margin 30.5% reported including tariff refunds, ~29.4% excluding vs GS estimate 28.9% and consensus 28.9%.
TGT 3Q26 SG&A ratio 21.9% reported vs GS estimate 21.5% and consensus 21.4%.

TGT 3Q26 EBIT $1.7bn reported including $301mn tariff refunds. Excluding refunds EBIT was $1,371mn, 5.1% margin, vs GS $1,256mn/4.7% and consensus $1,307mn/4.9%. Reported EBIT margin including refunds was 6.2%.

TGT FY26 guidance (company, issued with 3Q results): net sales growth around +6% (prior around +5%), EPS $10.65-11.40 including $2.14 of tariff refund benefits, or $8.51-9.26 excluding refunds (prior $8.25-9.25), operating margin around 6.2% including ~1.1 ppt of refunds (~5.1% excluding).
GS FY26 (1/27E) estimates before this print: EPS $8.79 (excluding refunds), revenue $110,271mn, EBIT $5,551.5mn. GS forecasts EPS $9.92 for 1/28E and $11.06 for 1/29E.
GS 4Q (1/27E) EPS estimate is $2.60 and 1Q27 (4/27E) is $2.00 (GS estimates, pre-print).
Tariff refunds contributed $301mn pretax, $228mn to net earnings and $0.50 to both GAAP and adjusted EPS in 3Q26. Company guidance excludes any potential future refunds.
risk_factors: Upside risks: improved macro backdrop lifting discretionary spending, incremental market share gains, and additional SG&A cost levers.

Downside risks: traffic and sales deceleration from weak consumer spending, inflation in product, freight and wage costs, a competitive environment forcing more aggressive pricing, and margin pressure from omni-channel and supply chain investment and mix shift.
